title: Deterministic acquire pipeline is never given a fetcher in production → never fetches or ingests anything
evidence: engine/cli/commands.py:1099 cmd_acquire calls run_acquire(run_cypher, write_cypher=..., cycle_id=..., apply=..., gap_limit=...) with NO fetcher= argument. engine/legion/commanders.py:69 _run_acquire passes fetcher=ctx.get('fetcher') but the legion ctx (commands.py cmd_legion ~1135) never sets ctx['fetcher']. In pipeline.py:37 `if fetcher is not None:` is therefore always False in production, so findings=() always. grep 'fetcher' over engine/cli/ returns only doc-comments and the parser help string — no code ever injects one.
fix: Wire a default real fetcher into cmd_acquire and the legion deterministic ctx — e.g. add a --web flag that injects WebSearchFetcher (already implemented) into run_acquire, and set ctx['fetcher'] in cmd_legion's deterministic path. Without a fetcher, gate --apply behind 'no fetcher → nothing to write'.
why: Prometheus's essence is external→KG ingest (fetch+extract+ingest), not just surfacing queries. As wired, every production invocation of the deterministic engine produces gaps+queries only and ingests 0 findings. The fetch→extract→ingest half of the pipeline exists and is tested but is unreachable through any real entry point.

title: CLI `acquire --apply` is structurally dead — can never write a :ResearchFinding
evidence: engine/cli/parser.py:410-414 exposes `--apply` with help 'Write :ResearchFinding (needs fetcher)'. But cmd_acquire (commands.py:1099) passes no fetcher, so findings is always empty and ingest_findings writes 0 (ingest.py:48 loops over empty findings). The user-facing help promises a write capability that the command can never perform from the CLI.
fix: Either add a fetcher source flag (--web → WebSearchFetcher) so --apply becomes functional, or have cmd_acquire print an explicit warning when --apply is set but no fetcher is available ('--apply ignored: no fetcher wired').
why: Dishonest/dead flag: a user running `bhgman acquire --apply --local` gets PROPOSE output and 0 writes with no error, despite --apply implying writes will happen. The 'needs fetcher' caveat is in help text but there is no flag or path to supply one.

title: LLM research path does real web search but never ingests to KG (PROPOSE-only), so essence's 'KG write' half is undelivered there too
evidence: engine/agents/prometheus.py:102 docstring: 'plan → N 병렬 리서치 → 합성. PROPOSE only (KG write 없음; /prom 보고 구조 그대로).' research() returns a ResearchReport with free-text synthesis and never calls write_cypher / ingest_findings. engine/legion/commanders.py:56-62 the llm branch returns {'mode':'llm','summary':...} with no ingest. why: Combined with finding #1: the deterministic path can ingest but never fetches; the LLM path fetches but never ingests. Neither production path delivers fetch→extract→ingest→KG-write end-to-end. The commander's stated essence (real ingest pipeline that persists acquired knowledge) is split across two paths and completed by neither.

title: MCP `prometheus_research` tool does no fetch/extract/ingest — returns a static plan dict only

title: No scheme allowlist on default fetch I/O → latent SSRF / local-file-read via untrusted DDG redirect
evidence: web.py:50-57 _unwrap_ddg returns the decoded `uddg` target verbatim with no scheme check (verified: _unwrap_ddg('/l/?uddg=file%3A%2F%2F%2Fetc%2Fpasswd') returns 'file:///etc/passwd'). web.py:25-32 _default_url_open calls urllib.request.urlopen on that string with no scheme restriction (noqa: S310 suppresses the bandit warning). The result links originate from an untrusted, self-described 'ToS-gray·구조 변화에 취약' HTML scrape.
fix: Restrict _default_url_open (and/or _unwrap_ddg) to http/https schemes; drop or skip any result link whose urlparse(scheme) not in {'http','https'}.
why: If WebSearchFetcher were wired (which the codebase intends, per its honest disclaimer and CallableFetcher seam), a manipulated/compromised DDG result page could redirect the fetcher to file:// or internal http endpoints, leaking local files or hitting intranet services. Currently low impact only because the fetcher is unwired (finding #5).

title: Shallow extraction silently drops claims beyond max_per_doc and has no test asserting truncation/empty-doc behavior
evidence: extract.py:71 `for claim in claims[:max_per_doc]` keeps only the first 2 substantive sentences per doc; a 3-sentence doc loses sentence 3 (verified: 3 sentences → 2 findings). There is no test for the truncation boundary, for docs that yield 0 substantive sentences (all below min_len), or for the run-on case where a doc with no sentence terminator becomes a single oversized claim (verified: 'word '*30 → 1 finding of 150 chars). The honest 'shallow extraction' disclaimer (extract.py:3) acknowledges weakness but tests don't pin the behavior.
fix: Add tests asserting: (a) exactly max_per_doc findings from a many-sentence doc, (b) 0 findings from an all-short-sentence doc, (c) the run-on/no-terminator fallback. Optionally make max_per_doc configurable from the pipeline/CLI.
why: extract_findings is the only point that turns fetched docs into structured findings; its truncation and degenerate-input behavior is load-bearing for completeness of ingested knowledge but is unverified, so a regression (e.g. changing the splitter or max_per_doc) would go uncaught.

title: nightly_drift_check.py never writes :DriftCheck / :ReinductionTrigger to the KG despite explicit docstring claim
evidence: engine/longinus_drift/nightly_drift_check.py:5-6 docstring: "emits a :DriftCheck record into the KG. If the gate fires, also emits a :ReinductionTrigger record". fix: Inject a KgClient (mirror sha256_baseline's DIP) and actually MERGE the emit_drift_check_record payload as a :DriftCheck node, plus a :ReinductionTrigger on fire. Add a test asserting the KG write occurs (MockKgClient.run_rows / a merge spy). At minimum, correct the docstring to say it prints-only until wired.
why: This is the designated nightly L8 re-induction trigger. Even once GDS is installed and the τ gate can fire, the system will only print to a log and never record the :DriftCheck audit trail or fire the :ReinductionTrigger the /prom 16 re-induction cycle depends on. The longinus 'KG persistence of drift' essence is silently absent on this path, and the docstring overstates delivered behavior.

title: Daemon watcher compares against in-process memory, not the KG baseline, and never emits drift to the KG
evidence: engine/longinus_drift_audit/daemon.py:17 docstring claims each child '├── compares with KG-stored baseline ├── emits drift events on change'. Actual _watcher_main (lines 135-156) compares each file's sha against a transient per-process dict `seen_hashes` (line 135), so it only detects 'changed since this watcher process started', NOT drift from the KG sha256_baseline. _drain_drift_queue (lines 277-286) only logger.info()s events — there is no KgClient anywhere in daemon.py (grep: 'KgClient' / 'emit_drift' / 'merge_reference' return nothing). daemon_cli.py wires `bhgman-daemon` as a real pyproject entry point (pyproject.toml:19).

Given the 'Skeleton' label this is a documented stub, but the specific KG-comparison claim must be corrected.
why: The shipped `bhgman-daemon` console script gives the impression of continuous KG-anchored drift watching, but it neither reads the KG baseline nor writes :SourceCodeDriftEvent. A file reverted to a drifted state across a daemon restart is undetected, and detected changes are lost on process exit. The advertised 'compares with KG-stored baseline' is false.

title: MCP backend misroutes legitimate READ Cypher to the write tool via naive substring keyword classification
evidence: engine/longinus_drift_audit/kg_client.py:480 `_MCP_WRITE_TOKENS = ("MERGE", "CREATE", "SET ", "DELETE", "REMOVE", "DETACH", "DROP", " SET\n")` and line 495 `tool = "write_neo4j_cypher" if any(t in up for t in _MCP_WRITE_TOKENS) else "read_neo4j_cypher"`. This is an unanchored substring match over the uppercased full query. Verified misclassification: `MATCH (n) RETURN n.preset` → 'write' (preset contains 'SET '), `MATCH (n {name:"asset manager"}) RETURN n` → 'write' ('asset '), `MATCH (n) WHERE n.name CONTAINS "create" RETURN n` → 'write' (literal CREATE). Path is `# pragma: no cover` (line 555) so untested.
fix: Classify by leading clause / token boundaries instead of substring: check whether the first non-comment keyword is one of MERGE/CREATE/DELETE/SET/REMOVE/DETACH/DROP, or strip string literals before scanning, or match `\bSET\b` etc. with word boundaries on the statement keywords only.
why: The generic run() escape hatch (used by DispatchAuditor for ad-hoc Cypher, dispatch_audit.py:123/193) can route a read query through the gateway's write tool when a property/literal contains a write keyword as a substring — causing spurious failures or, on a permission-segregated gateway, sending reads down a write-authorized channel. It silently undermines the read/write separation the MCP gateway is built around.

title: Several production-path modules have zero test coverage (nightly_drift_check, daemon watcher internals, refresh_drifted_baselines, daemon_cli)
evidence: Verified absence: nightly_drift_check (test_file='' , referenced_in_tests=0), refresh_drifted_baselines (0 refs), daemon_cli (0 refs). test_daemon.py only covers WatchConfig TOML parse + safe_read_hash + RepoEntry — the actual watcher behavior (_watcher_main change detection, _drain_drift_queue, _health_check auto-restart, _reconcile add/remove, LonginusDaemon.start) has no test. refresh_drifted_baselines.py performs live SET writes on every :ReferenceSite matching a drifted path with zero test.

title: Signature drift detector ignores default-value changes — a real API change goes undetected
evidence: engine/longinus_drift_audit/drift_detector.py:_parse_sig (lines 109-134) extracts only (param_name, annotation) pairs and the return annotation; default values are never captured. Verified: `_signatures_match('x: int = 0', 'x: int = 999')` returns True (no drift), while return/annotation/rename changes are correctly detected. The _parse_sig docstring (line 114) discloses '`*`/`/` markers are dropped — drift is judged on param identity + annotation + return', so default omission is a documented design choice but not mentioned for defaults specifically.
fix: Optionally include default-value source (ast.unparse of the default) in the _parse_sig tuple, or explicitly document in detect_sig_mismatch that default-value drift is out of scope so callers do not over-trust the signal.
why: Changing a function's default argument (e.g. a security-relevant `verify=True` → `verify=False`, or a tunable threshold) is a genuine behavioral API change that SigMismatch will report as clean, weakening the PutGet drift guarantee the detector advertises.

title: GED metric docstring overclaims algorithm (Hungarian/Riesen-Bunke) vs trivial set-difference implementation

The actual compute_ged (lines 32-62) is pure set difference: insertions=|kg_names - code_names|, deletions=|code_names - kg_names|, relabels=path mismatch on the intersection. The body does honestly add (lines 6-7) '본 prototype 은 간단한 label-based GED ... 실 production: networkx graph_edit_distance 위임 권장', so the disclosure exists lower down but the citation line misrepresents.

title: code_scanner parallel-threshold docstring is stale (says default 100, code is 5000)

README.md:113 also says default 5000.

title: Exact-duplicate supersession is a silent no-op but reported as successfully applied
evidence: kg_adapter.py:82-93 `_SUPERSEDE_CYPHER` matches stale and current both by `{sourcePath, sha256}`; with WHERE `stale <> current`. For a true exact duplicate (same path AND same sha — occam.py:57-59 `_reason` returns 'exact duplicate node (identical sha) — redundant', and occam.py emits it as a candidate), both MATCH clauses bind the identical key. Runtime trace: build_supersede params for the urdna2015 test case give stale_path==current_path AND stale_sha==current_sha (KEYS IDENTICAL? True). In Neo4j the `WHERE stale<>current` cross-product either supersedes BOTH nodes by each other or returns 0 rows; either way the intended single-archive is impossible. The kg_adapter.py:85 comment itself admits 'self-supersession 차단 (exact-dup 동일키 no-op)'. test_exact_duplicate_detected (test_occam.py:52-58) only checks the candidate is produced, never that build_supersede/apply produces a correct, distinguishing write.
fix: Disambiguate exact dups by a node-stable identity not in the composite key (e.g. add elementId()/id() of the chosen stale and current to the MATCH, fetched at read time), or special-case exact-dup candidates to use elementId-based supersession. At minimum, detect identical (stale,current) keys in build_supersede and refuse/flag rather than emit a no-op cypher counted as applied.
why: Exact byte-identical duplicate nodes are occam's flagship detection mode (mode-1) and a real observed case (urdna2015, ged_drift). The tool claims to archive them and reports applied_count>0, but the KG is never actually changed for these — the duplicates persist. This is exactly the kind of stale-node accumulation occam exists to remove, silently unhandled.

title: apply_supersessions reports applied_count without verifying the cypher actually changed anything
evidence: kg_adapter.py:154-164 `apply_supersessions`: `for (cypher, params), cand in zip(...): write_cypher(cypher, params); applied.append(_ident(cand.stale))` — it increments the applied list unconditionally, ignoring the rows the write returns. Runtime check: with a fake runner returning [] (0 rows, i.e. nothing matched/superseded, the exact-dup reality), res.applied_count == 1 and res.superseded == ('urdna.py',). The RETURN clause (kg_adapter.py:92) exists precisely to confirm what changed but is discarded.
fix: Have write_cypher return rows and count only candidates whose RETURN yields a superseded row; surface a mismatch (planned N vs actually-superseded M) in ApplyResult.notes. This makes the exact-dup no-op visible instead of hidden.
why: Violates the module's own honesty/numeric-claim discipline (CLAUDE.md 'Numeric claim spot-check'). The CLI prints `applied: <names>` and legion returns applied_count as the hygiene result, so users/orchestrator are told supersessions happened that did not. Compounds the exact-dup no-op into a dishonest report.

title: _pick_current is non-deterministic when same-path nodes have equal line_count
evidence: occam.py:48-54 `_pick_current` falls back to `max(group, key=lambda n: n.line_count)` (MEDIUM) when disk_sha is absent. Python's max returns the FIRST maximal element, so for two same-path nodes with equal line_count but different sha the 'current' depends on KG row order. Runtime: occam_pass([a,b]) picks current=a, occam_pass([b,a]) picks current=b (NON-DETERMINISTIC? True). KG MATCH row order is not guaranteed stable across runs.
fix: Add a deterministic tiebreak to _pick_current (e.g. on equal line_count, pick by sha256 or normalized name lexicographically), mirroring _pick_keep_drop.
why: occam archives the node it labels 'stale'. If two divergent same-size edits of one file both have nodes, occam may supersede whichever the query happened to return first — and a re-run can pick the opposite, flipping which real content gets archived. For an archive operation this is a correctness/idempotence hazard. semantic_dedup._pick_keep_drop (semantic_dedup.py:56-61) has a proper deterministic id tiebreak; occam's core does not.

title: Production path never supplies disk_truth, so the HIGH disk-sha confirmation is dead code and line-count heuristic is the sole arbiter of 'current'
evidence: grep for disk_truth across the whole repo (excluding engine/occam) returns nothing — no CLI (commands.py:853-859 calls run_occam without disk_truth), no legion (commanders.py:164-170), no efficacy caller passes it. occam_runner.py:5-6 docstring admits 'disk sha 확정(HIGH)이 필요하면 호출자가 disk_truth를 occam_pass에 직접 주입 (CLI 향후 enhancement).' Thus _pick_current's disk_sha branch (occam.py:50-53, the only thing producing HIGH confidence for mode-1) is never exercised in production; mode-1 always uses max(line_count) MEDIUM.
fix: Wire disk_truth in occam_runner: when repo_root is provided, hash on-disk files for same-path dup groups and pass disk_truth into occam_pass (the scan already walks the disk for disk_paths, so the files are in hand). Until then, document that mode-1 'current' selection is unconfirmed and downgrade auto-supersede of same-path different-sha dups to VERIFY.
why: For same-path duplicate nodes, occam decides which node is 'current' purely by line count, with no ground-truth check that the chosen current is the one actually on disk. A refactor that REDUCED line count leaves the real on-disk node with fewer lines than a stale bloated KG node, so occam would mark the actual current as stale and supersede it. The HIGH/MEDIUM Confidence enum advertised by the module is effectively MEDIUM-only in practice.

title: semantic_dedup default supersession key is nullable/non-unique 'name' — the exact regression #12 the kg_adapter explicitly moved away from
evidence: semantic_dedup.py:98 `def plan_supersession(pair, *, key: str = 'name')` and run_semantic_dedup default key='name' (semantic_dedup.py:137). The cypher (semantic_dedup.py:86-95) MATCHes `WHERE stale.{key} = $stale_id`. Meanwhile kg_adapter.py:77-81 documents the deliberate switch AWAY from name: 'name 단독 불가: (1) schema상 name은 required 아님 → null이면 MATCH 실패 + 다운스트림 None crash; (2) name 단독은 unique 아님' (KG challenge-occam-supersede-name-key-not-required-nullable-2026-06-02). The semantic path was not given the same fix. CLI does pass key from _SEMANTIC_TARGETS (commands.py:790,816), but the engine-level default and any direct caller inherit the nullable-name hazard.
fix: Make semantic_dedup require an explicit non-nullable unique key (default to 'findingId'/'id' for the relevant labels, or reject when key is 'name' unless caller affirms uniqueness), and assert the matched node count is 1 before writing, consistent with kg_adapter's composite-key rationale.
why: Lessons/Findings with null or duplicated `name` (precisely the nodes semantic dedup targets) will silently fail to MATCH (no supersession) or match multiple nodes (over-supersession), the same class of bug the kg_adapter regression already cost a fix for. Inconsistent identity policy across the two occam write paths is a latent correctness/drift risk.

title: Move/orphan disk-aware detection skips groups where any node lacks the repo marker, but a valid in-repo move with one abs and one external-looking path can be missed
evidence: occam.py:42-45 `_in_repo` returns True only if 'bhgman_tool/' substring is present; _detect_sha_moves (occam.py:71) and _detect_disk_orphans (occam.py:115) skip any node whose source_path lacks the marker. normalize_path (occam.py:34-39) returns the FULL path unchanged when the marker is absent, so such a node can never join disk_paths (which are all marker-stripped). This is intentional for genuinely external nodes (test_external_node_not_flagged_as_orphan), but it means a SourceCodeNode stored with a repo-relative path that does NOT contain the literal 'bhgman_tool/' segment (e.g. a path recorded as 'engine/foo.py' with no marker) is treated as external and excluded from move/orphan detection entirely.
fix: Make the repo marker configurable / accept paths already normalized to repo-relative form (treat a node whose path equals a disk_paths entry as in-repo even without the marker), or assert at ingestion that SourceCodeNode.sourcePath contains the marker.
why: The marker is the single load-bearing heuristic for 'is this node mine'. If KG ingestion ever records bare repo-relative paths without the bhgman_tool/ prefix, those nodes become invisible to occam's disk-aware modes — silent under-coverage rather than a wrong action. Lower severity because it degrades toward conservatism (no false supersession).

title: Goodhart cap rejects the strongest abstractions (stability=1.0) — pipeline kills its own best output
evidence: engine/eureka/quality_gate.py:60-70 applies GOODHART_CAP=0.95 to fca_stability; pipeline.py:343-353 computes avg_stability over induced concepts, passes it as evaluate(fca_stability=avg_stability), and `return pr` if not passed. Observed: run([], {node_a/b/c: frozenset({'axis_x','axis_y'})}, cfg) → '4.5-quality-gate' FAIL 'fca_stability 1.000 > Goodhart cap 0.95 — suspect artifact, reject'; stages reached = [...,'4.5-quality-gate'], never reaches '5-naesengmoon-gate'. Any tightly-cohesive cluster (objects sharing identical attribute sets — the strongest abstraction signal) yields FCA stability 1.0 and is rejected. Confirmed on '3 identical', '4 identical' contexts → stab 1.0.
fix: Do not apply the Goodhart cap to fca_stability (it is not a Goodhart-prone proxy). Either exempt fca_stability from the >GOODHART_CAP loop in quality_gate.evaluate, or have the pipeline gate per-concept (keep concepts with min_stability ≤ σ ≤ 1.0) instead of failing the whole batch on avg_stability. Add a test asserting a stability=1.0 concept survives to stage 5.
why: Eureka's essence is to surface repeated-pattern abstractions. The cleanest, most-confident concepts (perfect intent overlap) are exactly the ones the gate discards as 'artifact'. The Goodhart cap (Zaveri 2016) was meant for inflated proxy metrics (silhouette/modularity/AMI), not for FCA concept-stability, where σ=1.0 is a legitimate value for a fully-stable concept. In production (cmd_eureka / legion _run_induce both use default method='fca'), real KG abstractions with high stability are silently rejected, so eureka proposes nothing useful.

title: FCA induction is incomplete — only singleton-object closures, misses lattice meet-concepts
evidence: engine/eureka/induction_operators/fca.py:123-137 — induce_fca iterates `for obj in objects: extent,intent = _closure(frozenset({obj}), context)`, i.e. it only closes each single object. Observed on ctx {a:{x,y}, b:{x,z}, c:{x,y}}: induced concepts = [intent {x,y} extent {a,c}] only; the meet concept intent={x} extent={a,b,c} (grouping ALL three objects) is NEVER found (`any(c.intent==frozenset({'x'}))` → False). The module docstring (fca.py:1-18) claims 'Ganter-Wille 1999 fundamental theorem', 'concept-lattice', and 'iceberg-lattice (Roth-Obiedkov-Kourie 2008)' bounding — implying full lattice enumeration.
fix: Compute the full set of intents via attribute-closures too (close each attribute and each pairwise intent intersection), or use a standard NextClosure/iceberg enumeration so meet-concepts appear. At minimum, downgrade the docstring/README claim from 'Galois lattice' to 'object-concept enumeration' and document the omission. Add a test with overlapping-but-distinct attribute sets asserting the meet concept is produced.
why: The whole value of FCA over naive clustering is the concept LATTICE — meet/join concepts that group objects by shared sub-attributes. By enumerating only object-atoms, the operator silently drops the broader abstractions (the most general groupings) that are eureka's core deliverable, and the README's 'Galois lattice' claim is overstated relative to what the code computes.

title: Flagship pipeline test name 'runs_to_completion' is false — passes while pipeline halts at stage 4.5
evidence: engine/eureka/tests/test_pipeline.py:5-19 test_pipeline_runs_to_completion_with_fca_input uses context {node_a/b/c: frozenset({'axis_x','axis_y'})} and only asserts '4-induce-fca' ran with abstract_classes>=1. Observed: that exact context HALTS at '4.5-quality-gate' (stability 1.0 > Goodhart cap) and never reaches '5-naesengmoon-gate' — yet the test passes. No pipeline test asserts the run reaches stage 5 / produces VERDICT_PENDING acs, and PipelineRun stores only StageResult count summaries (the 5-gate payload is {} for empty acs), so the actual AbstractClass objects are unretrievable from a successful end-to-end run.
fix: Add a true end-to-end test with a context whose concept survives all gates, asserting '5-naesengmoon-gate' is reached and gated acs are VERDICT_PENDING. Rename the existing test or fix the gate so the named scenario truly runs to completion. Consider exposing the proposed AbstractClass objects on PipelineRun so callers/하데스 can retrieve them.
why: The misleading test name and shallow assertion mask the Goodhart-cap bug and the fact that no test exercises the full induce→quality→oracle→fidelity→gate→validator path with a surviving concept. The module appears '114 passing' but its core happy path (concept actually proposed) has zero coverage.

title: avg_stability batch coupling — one perfect concept rejects an entire good batch
evidence: engine/eureka/pipeline.py:343-353 — the quality gate is evaluated once on avg_stability over the whole batch, not per-concept. Observed: acs with stabilities [1.0, 0.96] → avg 0.98 → evaluate(fca_stability=0.98).passed == False (Goodhart). A single high-stability concept drags the batch mean above the cap and rejects co-occurring legitimate concepts. Additionally, leiden-llm/leiden-true stability (internal-edge cohesion ratio, leiden_llm.py:160-163) is fed into the fca_stability slot regardless of operator (pipeline.py:344), conflating a graph-cohesion metric with the FCA Galois-stability threshold.
fix: Gate per-concept (filter the acs list) rather than on the batch average, and pass operator-appropriate metrics into evaluate() (e.g. modularity for Leiden, fca_stability only for FCA). Remove or scope the Goodhart cap as in finding 1.
why: Batch-level averaging makes concept acceptance depend on unrelated sibling concepts in the same run, which is non-local and surprising; combined with the Goodhart cap it amplifies the false-rejection problem. The metric mislabel (cohesion ratio → fca_stability) means the documented FCA_STABILITY_MIN threshold semantics don't actually hold for the Leiden operators.

title: Dead/unused header regex in AMIE3 parser
evidence: engine/eureka/induction_operators/amie3.py:80-83 defines _RULE_HEADER_PAT (a precompiled regex for the AMIE table header), but _parse_rules (line 86-124) uses an ad-hoc inline substring check `if 'Head Coverage' in line and 'PCA Confidence' in line` instead. title: KG-realization pipeline is dead: eureka never writes the `verdictStatus='ACCEPTED'` that hades queries for
evidence: engine/hades/hades_runner.py:24-27 `_FETCH_ALL` filters `WHERE a.verdictStatus = 'ACCEPTED' AND (a.status IS NULL OR a.status <> 'CANONICAL')`. But `grep -rn verdictStatus engine/ --include=*.py` (non-test) returns ONLY hades_runner.py and kg_local/runner.py — eureka NEVER writes it. eureka's canonical model engine/eureka/induction_models.py:35-40 has `status` enum = PROPOSED/VERDICT_PENDING/CANONICAL/CANONICAL_DELEGATED/REJECTED (no `ACCEPTED`, no `verdictStatus` field), and pipeline.py:139 emits `status=AbstractClassStatus.PROPOSED`, stage_5 (pipeline.py:299-301) only bumps to VERDICT_PENDING. eureka pipeline/models/stages contain no MERGE/persist/to_cypher at all. So in the legion chain (창조 eureka → 검증 → 실현 hades, legion/commanders.py:287-300) hades's fetch returns 0 rows against any KG eureka actually populated.
fix: Pick ONE property name and reconcile both ends: either change hades_runner._FETCH_ALL/_FETCH_ONE to filter on eureka's actual field (`a.status='ACCEPTED'` after adding an ACCEPTED value to AbstractClassStatus and a fidelity/judgment gate that transitions PROPOSED→ACCEPTED and writes it to KG), or add a real eureka KG-persist stage that emits `verdictStatus`. Add an integration test that runs eureka pipeline → persists → hades fetch and asserts >0 candidates, instead of relying on the mirrored local fixture.
why: hades's entire reason to exist on the KG axis (realize ACCEPTED abstractions eureka proposed) is unreachable end-to-end. The tests/legion only pass because engine/kg_local/runner.py:87 hand-mirrors the exact `verdictStatus=='ACCEPTED'` predicate in the local fixture — a tautology that hides the broken producer→consumer contract. The 'dual of eureka' claim is not delivered for KG realization.

title: _find_classdef silently returns the WRONG class when the requested name is absent but the file has exactly one class
evidence: engine/hades/extract_superclass.py:90-99: after no name match, `any_cls = [...ClassDef...]; return any_cls[0] if len(any_cls) == 1 else None`. Observed: `_find_classdef('class Wolf:\n def speak...', 'Dog')` returns the `Wolf` classdef (printed `asked for Dog, got: Wolf`). This propagates through `_lifted` (extract_superclass.py:102-111) so extract_superclass/realize_code_extract_superclass will lift methods using a class the caller never named.
fix: Remove the single-class fallback (return None when the named class is not found), or require the key to equal cd.name. At minimum log/raise on name!=requested. Add a test: class_sources={'Dog': '<source defining Wolf>'} must return None, not a Wolf-based patch.
why: A mislabeled class_sources entry (e.g. wrong key→source mapping from the CLI scan) yields a confidently-wrong superclass patch over an unrelated class, with no error. Realization must be faithful; silently binding to the wrong donor violates the covenant of fidelity and could generate an incorrect refactor that the diff/test gate may still pass if the bodies happen to match.

title: INSTANCE_OF realization op matches members by name with NO label, risking binding to arbitrary/unrelated nodes
evidence: engine/hades/hades.py:67-73 op[1]: `UNWIND $members AS m MATCH (a:AbstractClass {name:$concept}) MATCH (o {name:m}) MERGE (o)-[:INSTANCE_OF]->(a)`. `MATCH (o {name:m})` has no label constraint, so any node in the graph whose `name` equals a member string gets an INSTANCE_OF edge — including unrelated nodes that share a name, or self if a member name collides with $concept. No test covers wrong-label/overmatch (grep of tests shows only injection + named-AbstractClass regression checks).
fix: Constrain the member match to the intended member label(s), e.g. `MATCH (o:ReferenceSite {name:m})` or pass an expected label/elementId list from eureka's extent rather than bare names. Add a test asserting a same-named node of a different label is NOT bound.
why: On a real Neo4j KG with name collisions across labels, hades --apply will create spurious INSTANCE_OF edges, corrupting the ontology it is meant to faithfully materialize. The undo (hades.py:75-76) deletes `MATCH (o)-[r:INSTANCE_OF]->(a:AbstractClass {name:$concept})` so it would clean spurious edges too, but the forward op still pollutes during apply and can attach members of the wrong kind.

title: ast-backend `unified_diff` is misleadingly noisy — claims 'human-reviewable real diff' but shows reformatting unrelated to the lift
evidence: engine/hades/extract_superclass.py:114-128 `_build_diff` compares raw `before` text to `ast.unparse`-canonicalized `after`. Observed on `class Dog:  # a dog\n    x=1\n    def speak...`: the diff shows `-    x=1 / +    x = 1` and drops the `# a dog` comment as if the refactor changed them — but those are pure ast.unparse canonicalization, not the Extract-Superclass operation. extract_superclass.py:11-12 docstring acknowledges canonicalization but the field is still named `unified_diff` and CLI --show-patch prints it as the review artifact (commands.py:1038-1039).
fix: For the ast backend, normalize `before` through the same ast.unparse round-trip before diffing (so only the lift shows), or default the CLI/diff to the cst (format-preserving) backend, and document the diff as canonicalized when ast is used.
why: hades is supposed to produce a faithful, reviewable realization. A reviewer reading the ast-backend diff cannot distinguish the actual lift from formatting churn, undermining the 'apply 전 characterization test' review step and inviting accidental approval of unintended changes.

title: Harness diagnose engine forces name-matched primitives PRESENT, contradicting its own honesty notes and ignoring negating free-text
evidence: engine/harness/harness.py:131-138 _classify_tier returns a framework's hardcoded primitive axes on any name substring match; _axis_finding (harness.py:150-151) marks those axes PRESENT 'framework primitive' unless an explicit signals dict overrides. Observed: `diagnose('claude code with no hooks and no tests at all')` → present axes ['CONSTRAIN','VERIFY']. Meanwhile diagnose's own notes[2] (harness.py:167) says 'framework→축 매핑은 주관적 휴리스틱 KB(미검증 단정)' and the module docstring (harness.py:8-13) admits axis assignment is '빌더의 해석'. So the engine asserts capabilities it simultaneously labels unverified.
fix: Demote framework-primitive axes to a lower-confidence presence (e.g. an INFERRED/Presence value distinct from signal-PRESENT), and let negating free-text or absence of corroborating keyword reduce confidence. At minimum surface the conflict in the AxisFinding.signal.
why: The harness diagnosis is the *passive 場 측면* of hades=harness; emitting PRESENT for a stripped-down instance that explicitly lacks the capability is a dishonest verdict that the module's own notes disclaim. A consumer trusting `present_axes` gets false positives.

title: Two divergent harness-diagnosis implementations: engine/harness (real) vs MCP tool skeleton with permanently 'unknown' axes
evidence: engine/harness/harness.py uses tiers IDE_HOST/RUNTIME/MANAGED_CLOUD with computed 4-axis findings, while engine/mcp_server/tools/harness.py:19-39 KNOWN_INSTANCES uses a different tier vocab (L_IDE/L_RT/L_MC), is a hardcoded lookup, and harness_diagnose_impl (lines 48-101) ALWAYS returns axes all 'unknown' with note 'Skeleton classifier ... Production classifier in Phase 2'. The MCP tool does not import or delegate to the real engine/harness.diagnose. server.py:32/43 registers this skeleton as the live `harness_diagnose` MCP tool.
fix: Have engine/mcp_server/tools/harness.harness_diagnose_impl delegate to engine.harness.diagnose() and map its tiers/axes into the report shape, deleting the duplicate KNOWN_INSTANCES skeleton, or document that the MCP tool is intentionally a stub and remove the 'Phase 2' promise. This is both an unfinished gap on the MCP path and KG/vocab drift (L_IDE vs IDE_HOST) that will confuse downstream consumers.

title: realize_code_template is a dead-but-shipped symbolic stub superseded by the real engine, yet still exported and tested as if a realization path
evidence: engine/hades/hades.py:91-122 realize_code_template only builds string ops like `f"EXTRACT shared template '{lgg_template}' → ..."` and `f"REPLACE site {s} ..."` — no code is generated; it is the 'symbolic plan' the docstring of extract_superclass.py:3 explicitly says was REPLACED by the real engine. It remains in __all__ (hades.py:184-190) and has tests (test_hades.py:77-87) asserting only that it returns PLANNED strings. No caller in CLI/legion uses it (CLI uses realize_code_extract_superclass / extract_superclass).
fix: Either remove realize_code_template (and its tests) now that the real ast engine exists, or rename it to make its symbolic-only nature explicit (e.g. plan_code_template) and document it as a non-realizing planner.
why: A function that only emits human-readable strings about a refactor sits in the public API next to the real realizer with near-identical naming (realize_code_template vs realize_code_extract_superclass), inviting callers to use the fake one and get no actual realization. Tests give it false legitimacy.

title: lean-goals oracle counts sorry/admit inside comments, underreporting closed goals behind a passing gate
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/oracle_adapters.py:29 `_LEAN_HOLE = re.compile(r"\b(sorry|admit)\b")` then line 58 `return float(len(_LEAN_DECL.findall(src)) - len(_LEAN_HOLE.findall(src)))`. Observed: a file `-- this proof avoids sorry\ntheorem t : True := trivial\n/- admit ... -/` compiles (lean exit 0) but scores 1 decl - 2 holes = -1.0. Contrast: the SAME repo's axiom_audit.py:27 deliberately uses comment-aware `_SORRY = re.compile(r"(?::=|by)\s+sorry\b")` with a test asserting 'sorry in a comment does not count' (test_truth_lenses.py:36-41). The fitness-critical oracle uses the naive regex.
fix: Strip Lean comments (`--` to EOL and `/- ... -/` nesting) before applying _LEAN_HOLE/_LEAN_DECL, or reuse axiom_audit's proof-position-anchored _SORRY regex. Add a test: a clean theorem with 'sorry'/'admit' in comments must score the true closed-goal count, not be penalized.
why: lean-goals is the module's flagship 'substrate-disjoint, can't-be-faked' oracle and the fitness signal for evolve_loop. A valid, fully-closed proof that merely mentions 'sorry'/'admit' in prose comments gets a corrupted (often negative) score behind an exit-0 gate, so the deterministic oracle silently lies about how many goals a candidate closed — directly degrading the verification honesty the lens exists to provide.

title: n_eff anti-inflation safeguard bypassed for a single judgment critic — lone LLM lens yields a clean PASS
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/decorrelation.py:138-149 `_verdict_label`: branch order checks `if all_pass and adjusted >= 0.90: return 'PASS'` BEFORE `if n_eff < 1.5 and n_oracle == 0: return 'CONDITIONAL_PASS'`. For one judgment critic with PASS: shrink = n_eff/participating = 1.0/1 = 1.0, so adjusted = raw(1.0)*1.0 = 1.0 >= 0.90 → returns clean 'PASS' with n_eff=1.0, n_oracle=0. Verified: `aggregate([CriticVerdict('a',JUDGMENT,True,'claude')], rho=0.0).verdict == 'PASS'`. No test covers the single-judgment-critic verdict (test_decorrelation.py only tests 3-critic correlated, oracle+judgment, all-fail).
fix: Make the 'no oracle ⇒ no clean PASS' invariant precede the all_pass shortcut, e.g. require `n_oracle >= 1` (or n_eff >= 2 with at least one oracle) for a 'PASS'; otherwise cap at CONDITIONAL_PASS. Add a test asserting a single judgment critic (and a 2-critic ρ=0 judgment-only ensemble) never returns clean PASS.
why: The module's entire stated thesis (docstring lines 1-12, and the line-146 comment 'correlated judgment only → capped, never a clean PASS') is that LLM judgment alone must never be read as independent confidence. The n=1 case — exactly a single self-review lens — escapes the cap and rubber-stamps a clean PASS, reintroducing the rubber-stamp/over-confidence the lens was built to prevent.

title: axiom-taint transitive closure silently fails on dotted/namespaced Lean imports
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/axiom_audit.py:25 `_IMPORT = re.compile(r"^import\s+([\w.]+)")` captures the full dotted path (e.g. 'Bhgman.Base'), but _tainted_stems (line 63) matches `any(imp in tainted for imp in p.sibling_imports if imp in by_stem)` where by_stem keys are bare file stems (line 41 path.stem). Observed: `import Bhgman.Base` on a file importing an axiom-tainted Base.lean leaves the importer UNtainted — axiom_resting_theorems=1 instead of 2. Only bare-stem imports (`import Base`) are tested (test_truth_lenses.py:24). Repo lean/ currently uses bare stems so the bug is latent but activates on any namespaced import.
fix: Normalize captured imports to their final dotted segment (or match by full module path) before the `imp in by_stem` test, since a file's Lean module name is its stem but imports reference it as a (possibly namespaced) module path. Add a test with `import Pkg.Base` taint propagation.
why: This lens exists to honestly separate axiom-tainted theorems from axiom-free ones (external review tension #1). A broken transitive closure UNDERSTATES axiom dependence — the dangerous direction — letting axiom-resting theorems be reported as 'axiom-free (Lean's own foundation)', the exact overclaim the lens audits others for. The docstring claims '전이 폐쇄: import한 게 tainted면 나도 tainted' as an invariant.

title: estimate_rho never called in production — aggregate always uses the static DEFAULT_RHO prior
evidence: grep for estimate_rho outside tests/decorrelation.py returns only engine/naesengmoon/__init__.py (re-export). The sole production caller, engine/legion/commanders.py:240 `ens = aggregate(critics)`, passes no rho → decorrelation.py:162 falls back to `DEFAULT_RHO=0.7`. No probe/known-answer vote matrix is ever built or measured.
fix: Either wire a small known-answer probe set through estimate_rho in commanders._run_verify and pass the measured rho into aggregate, or honestly relabel the prior path (DEFAULT_RHO) as 'assumed, unmeasured' in the summary string so the n_eff value isn't read as empirical.
why: The decorrelation module advertises MEASURED effective independence (estimate_rho via Pearson over a shared probe set, docstring lines 86-97), but the production verdict always assumes a fixed ρ=0.7 prior regardless of the actual critics' correlation. n_eff is therefore a constant-prior estimate dressed as a measured one; the 'honest measured independence' capability is dead at the production boundary.

title: occam-twins oracle drops repo_root through verify()/cmd_oracle — only same-path duplicates detected
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/oracle_adapters.py:117 `occam_twins_oracle(run_cypher, scope=None, repo_root=None)` forwards repo_root to run_occam, but engine/naesengmoon/verify.py:67 calls `occam_twins_oracle(run_cypher, scope)` with no repo_root, and verify() has no repo_root parameter; engine/cli/commands.py:925 sets `kwargs = {'run_cypher': ..., 'scope': args.scope}` only. run_occam (occam_runner.py:96-102) docstring: 'repo_root 주면 ... disk-orphan(mode-2/3) 탐지 활성. None이면 same-path 중복(mode-1)만.'
fix: Add a repo_root parameter to verify() and a `--repo-root` arg to cmd_oracle, forwarding to occam_twins_oracle; default to the repo root so disk-truth (mode-2/3) detection is active by default.
why: Invoked through the canonical verify surface / `bhgman-tool oracle --kind occam-twins`, the occam oracle silently runs in its weakest mode — it cannot see sha-move or disk-orphan supersessions and reports fewer stale duplicates than actually exist. A clean PASS (score==0) is then unjustified completeness, undermining the oracle's stated 'lossless dead-node' coverage.

title: falsifiability priority order demotes genuinely truth-apt empirical/efficacy claims to 'consistency-only / not truth-apt'
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/falsifiability.py:91 classify priority is unfalsifiable > consistency > efficacy > empirical. Observed: classify('APT is 2x faster and the proof type-checks') → claim_class='consistency-only', truth_apt=False; classify('this benchmark shows the theorem passes') → consistency-only/False; classify('our method beats baseline and is consistent') → consistency-only/False. Any consistency keyword ('theorem','passes','consistent','compiles') wins and strips truth_apt even when an empirical/efficacy falsifier exists.
fix: When a claim matches BOTH a consistency hint and an empirical/efficacy hint, prefer the truth-apt route (or return a multi-class routing) rather than silently collapsing to consistency-only. At minimum reorder so empirical/efficacy (truth_apt=True) is not overridden by an incidental consistency keyword.
why: The lens's purpose (external review tension #4) is to route truth-apt claims to the cheapest EXTERNAL falsifier. The consistency-first precedence routes testable empirical claims AWAY from external falsification (demotes to 'PASS = consistent-given-axioms, NOT true'), the wrong direction. The docstring disclaims classifier precision but not this directional demotion of truth-apt claims.

title: prompt_echo_score normalizes by executor-hint size, so short hints trivially flag critics as echo-suspect
evidence: engine/naesengmoon/decorrelation.py:110-119 `prompt_echo_score` returns `len(hb & cb) / len(hb)` (overlap coefficient over the HINT's bigrams). With a short executor_hint (few bigrams), a critic that happens to restate any of them exceeds ECHO_THRESHOLD=0.65 and is excluded from the n_eff tally via flag_echo. test_flag_echo_marks_suspect uses a 4-word hint where one shared phrase flips the flag.
fix: Use a symmetric Jaccard (|hb∩cb|/|hb∪cb|) or require a minimum hint bigram count before the echo test fires, and add a test for a short-hint non-echo critic that must NOT be flagged.
why: Echo-exclusion shrinks the judgment tally and lowers n_eff/coverage; over-eager flagging on short executor hints (the common case for a one-line claim) can drop legitimately-independent critics, biasing the ensemble toward CONDITIONAL/FAIL. It is a quieter failure than the n=1 PASS bug but still distorts the honest-independence accounting.

title: KG-anchored DAG/cycle decomposition is silently fail-closed-BLOCKED (essence gap on the --anchor path)
evidence: kg_adapter.py:33 `_CHILDREN_CYPHER` traverses `-[:DECOMPOSES_TO|HAS_CHILD|DEPENDS_ON]->(c)` (DEPENDS_ON forms arbitrary digraphs), but planner.plan()/walk() and kg_decompose() have NO visited-set. Observed: a diamond KG (span-root→a,b; a→shared; b→shared) yields seeds ['...root','...a','...shared','...b','...shared'] → invariants fire DUP_SEED_NAME + 2×E3_MULTIPLE_SEED_PER_ANCHOR → run_jaebaeman blocks the whole plan: notes=('BLOCKED by 3 invariant violation(s) — write 차단 (fail-closed)',), dry_run=True. A KG cycle a→b→a produces duplicate seeds ['...a','...b','...a','...b'] (only saved from infinite recursion by max_depth=3) → same DUP_SEED_NAME block. No test in engine/jaebaeman/tests/ exercises a DAG/diamond/cycle in the decomposition source; all KG tests use pure trees (test_runner.py:32, test_invariants.py:100).
fix: Add a visited-set (by node name) in kg_decompose/plan so a shared node is only expanded once and emitted once (collapse DAG to a per-name-unique seed set, which is exactly what the downstream MERGE is idempotent on), or explicitly detect cycles/diamonds and emit a dedicated diagnostic + dedupe instead of a generic DUP/E3 block. Add DAG and cycle tests for the kg_decompose path.
why: The --anchor / KG-structure decomposition is the headline non-trivial path of the commander (plan-first over real KG structure). Real KG decomposition graphs routinely contain shared sub-spans (diamonds) and DEPENDS_ON cycles, so the most useful inputs are exactly the ones that cannot be planted at all. The failure is also misleading: it surfaces as a 1:1-ownership 'violation' rather than an unsupported-DAG diagnostic.

title: _assert_covenant guards are tautological — they only validate hardcoded constant templates
evidence: kg_adapter.py:174/194/207 call `_assert_covenant(_SEED_MERGE)` / `(_HAS_SEED_EDGE)` / `(_DECOMPOSES_TO_EDGE)` and lifecycle.py:91 calls `_assert_covenant(_STATUS_SET)` — always passing a fixed module-level string that by construction never contains DELETE/DETACH/REMOVE. The assert can never fail for any caller input. The injected `write_cypher`/`run_cypher` runner (the only thing that could actually carry a destructive op) is never checked.
fix: Either move the covenant check to the actual write boundary (wrap write_cypher so every cypher string passed to the runner is token-checked), or remove the tautological asserts and document that destructive-op prevention relies on the fixed templates only. Add a test that a destructive runner/cypher is actually rejected.
why: The MERGE-only / no-destructive-op 'covenant' is advertised as a load-bearing safety invariant ('씨앗은 심기만, 뽑지 않음') and is even unit-tested, but the guard provides false assurance: it asserts a constant against itself. If anyone later parametrizes the cypher or routes a different statement through the same builder, nothing catches it.

title: Coinductive mode leaves PlanResult.plan as a root-only frontier stub while seeds contains the full tree
evidence: jaebaeman_runner.py:66 `tree = pairs[0][0]` — in coinductive mode each lazy node has children=() (frontier), so the returned PlanResult.plan is only the root. Observed: a 3-node coinductive plan returns seeds=['seed-jaebaeman-g','seed-jaebaeman-a','seed-jaebaeman-b'] but walk(res.plan) yields only ['g']. depth_max/leaf_count are computed separately from pairs so they stay correct (jaebaeman_runner.py:68-69).
fix: Reconstruct the nested PlanNode tree from the (node, parent) pairs for the coinductive branch (or document PlanResult.plan as 'frontier root only in coinductive mode' and have telemetry/consumers use seeds, not plan).
why: Any consumer that introspects result.plan (visualization, a future telemetry path, or external callers doing walk(res.plan)) sees a tree inconsistent with res.seeds. It is an internal honesty/consistency gap: two fields of the same result describe different trees.

title: Legion substrate maps stage outcomes to seeds by positional index without verifying verb identity
evidence: engine/legion/jaebaeman_substrate.py:51-58 `outcomes_to_seed_outcomes` zips `leaf_seeds[i]` to `stage_ocs[i]` by index. leaf_seeds order comes from default_stages() verb order; stage_ocs order comes from run.outcomes (CANONICAL_ORDER). They are equal today (verified: both = ['획득','연결','창조','정리','검증','실현']) but nothing asserts the pairing — neither the function nor test_jaebaeman_substrate.py checks that seed i's verb matches outcome i's verb.
fix: Match seed↔outcome by verb (build leaf seeds keyed on verb, look up the StageOutcome with the same verb) and assert lengths/verbs align; add a test that shuffled stage order still maps correctly.
why: If default_stages() ordering or CANONICAL_ORDER ever diverges, every stage outcome gets silently mis-attributed to the wrong commander seed (e.g. 검증's success recorded under 정리's seed) with green tests, corrupting the audit RunRecord/lifecycle status. Position-coupling is a latent drift trap.

title: Coinductive fuel-truncation reports unexpanded frontier nodes as leaves in leaf_count
evidence: jaebaeman_runner.py:68-69 computes leaf_count_v via `id(n) not in has_child`. With fuel-bounded BFS, a node whose children were never enqueued (cut by fuel) has no recorded child and is counted as a leaf. Observed: branching=2/depth=3 tree, coinductive fuel=3 → seeds [g, g.0, g.1], leaf_count=2 even though g.0/g.1 have children in the source tree (they are frontier, not true leaves).
fix: Distinguish frontier nodes from true leaves in coinductive mode (e.g. only count a node as leaf if its decompose() returned empty AND it was within fuel/depth budget), or rename/annotate the metric as 'frontier_count' when fuel-bounded.
why: leaf_count is part of the audit surface (RunRecord/telemetry, PlanResult.summary 'leaves=N'). In fuel-truncated runs it conflates 'frontier (not yet expanded)' with 'genuine leaf', overstating how complete the plan is. Misleading for any downstream completeness check.

title: Measurement-driven conditional dispatch is fully built and tested but wired into NOTHING — the orchestrator runs a fixed order
evidence: Repo-wide grep: `decide_dispatch` and `.measure()` (engine/legion/measurement.py:188,199) have ZERO non-test, non-self callers. The real orchestrator engine/legion/legion.py:54-95 Legion.run() iterates self._stages in registration order and never imports measurement.py, never calls measure() or decide_dispatch(); commanders.py:287-306 hardcodes the 6-stage CANONICAL_ORDER. The `legion` CLI (commands.py:1159 run_legion_via_jaebaeman) and `apt --gated` (commands.py:279-301 build_default_legion+run_gated) both run that fixed pipeline. So per-commander self-measurement → threshold-gated need detection → conditional invocation (the canonical essence per 7cmd-measurement-driven-conditional-dispatch-2026-05-30 and SPEC 7CMD_NEED_BASED_DISPATCH_SPEC.md) does not occur at runtime.
fix: Either (a) make Legion.run()/commanders consult CommanderBase.measure()+decide_dispatch() to dynamically insert/skip stages and emit DispatchDecision/DispatchEvent records, or (b) if static order is the intended production behavior, demote measurement.py/threshold_derivation to an explicitly-labeled experimental/spec module and correct all docstrings & KG claims that assert runtime measurement-driven dispatch.
why: The module is literally titled and documented as delivering measurement-driven conditional dispatch (measurement.py:1-8, README 'need-based dispatch'). In reality dispatch is a static compile-time sequence — the exact 'fixed USES edge' the user explicitly RETRACTED on 2026-05-30. The commander's core essence is not delivered; an entire well-tested subsystem is dead code relative to the running product.

title: G2_ADVERSARY_RAN reports PASS even when the naesengmoon verdict is oracle=FAIL / ensemble=REJECT
evidence: gated_run.py:81-89 eval_g2_adversary_ran only checks StageOutcome.ok. legion.py:79 sets ok=True for any stage that returns its declared provides keys. commanders.py:_run_verify ALWAYS returns {'verdict': {...}} regardless of outcome — verified live: with a degraded upstream, _run_verify returns verdict.oracle='FAIL', verdict.ensemble='FAIL', yet the integration run prints `G2_ADVERSARY_RAN PASS — naesengmoon 검증 ran and passed`. The gate conflates 'the verify stage executed and returned a dict' with 'the adversary passed'.
fix: eval_g2_adversary_ran must inspect the verify stage's actual verdict content from final context (verdict.oracle != 'FAIL' AND verdict.ensemble not in {'REJECT','FAIL'}), not merely StageOutcome.ok. Add an integration test asserting G2=FAIL when verdict.oracle/ensemble is FAIL/REJECT.
why: gated_run.py is the north-star 'APT-zero' runtime whose docstring (lines 9-14) promises G2 = 'a different lens looked AND passed = auditability' and fail-closed honesty ('refuses to certify what it cannot check'). A run the adversary REJECTED still earns G2 PASS, defeating the audit gate and the honesty claim the whole runtime is built to make.

title: hades realization gates only on oracle FAIL — an ensemble REJECT verdict still realizes (writes to KG)
evidence: commanders.py:256 `if verdict.get('oracle') == 'FAIL': return skipped`. Verified live: with ctx verdict={'oracle':'PASS','ensemble':'REJECT'}, _run_realize returns mode='hades' (proceeds to run_hades CANONICAL+INSTANCE_OF write), not 'skipped'. The judgment ensemble verdict that _run_verify computes via decorrelation.aggregate/flag_echo/n_eff (commanders.py:237-248) is never consulted by the realization gate.

why: The module docstring (commanders.py:18) states '검증(나생문) 통과 후에만 추상→구체 내려보냄 (나생문 gate 후)'. Only the deterministic oracle half gates; the adversarial LLM-critic half is purely advisory. When LLM enrichment is active and critics reject a synthesized abstraction, hades still writes it as CANONICAL — exactly the GAN-D bypass the verification commander exists to prevent.

title: threshold_derivation subpackage (1157 LOC) + thresholds.toml externalization are never consumed by the dispatch engine
evidence: config.py:1-15 documents it 'externalizes the 14 hardcoded measurement.py thresholds ... read at runtime (no code edit for tuning)', but load_thresholds() (config.py:54) has zero production callers (grep: thresholds.toml referenced only inside config.py itself). measurement.py CommanderBase subclasses still hardcode every threshold as class-attribute DispatchThreshold tuples (e.g. measurement.py:248 value=16, :258 0.3, :294 0.5). grep for 'DispatchThreshold|dispatch_thresholds' inside threshold_derivation/ = 0 hits: no derived value (roc_youden/bayesian_map/cusum) ever flows back into a runtime threshold. config.py's own precedence list ends with '#4 measurement.py hardcoded fallback' — which is the ONLY path ever taken.
fix: Wire config.load_thresholds() into CommanderBase so dispatch_thresholds resolve from TOML (falling back to hardcoded), and have threshold_derivation outputs write the TOML with real derived_at_cycle provenance. Or explicitly label the subpackage as offline/experimental and stop claiming runtime externalization in config.py docstring.

This is a large surface of effort with no load-bearing path — drift between claimed and actual capability.

title: DispatchInstrumentLog ground-truth outcome logging has no production caller — dispatch decisions are never instrumented
evidence: measurement.py:145-175 set_instrument_log/record_outcome exist with comment 'PROM 16 P3(a) wire'. Repo-wide non-test grep for set_instrument_log/record_outcome: only definitions in measurement.py plus backfill_kg.py (a one-shot historical backfill script). Combined with finding #1 (decide_dispatch never runs), there are no real DispatchDecisions to instrument.

title: Stevens-scale 'bug fix' tests assert on metrics that no measure() ever emits (dead scale entries)

title: README mislabels audit_prom_cycles.py as 'HMAC tamper-evident audit' and omits half the module
evidence: engine/legion/README.md lists 'audit_prom_cycles.py — HMAC tamper-evident audit', but that file (audit_prom_cycles.py) does Stevens-scale violation scanning of PROM finding JSONs and contains zero HMAC code (grep -c hmac = 0). title: OPA adapter only reads `allow`; break_glass/kg_admission/taliban policies (allow_override/allow_mutation/approve) always deny
evidence: engine/gate/gate_endpoint.py:266-277 `_eval_opa` does `allow = bool(result.get("allow", False))`. But the mapped Rego policies define different rule names: break_glass.rego:11/23 `default allow_override := false` / `allow_override if`; kg_mutations/admission_control.rego:14/74 `allow_mutation`; taliban/constitutional_9.rego:24/26 `approve`. `_GATE_POLICY` (gate_endpoint.py:244-255) routes gate_name `break_glass`/`kg_admission`/`taliban`/`naesengmoon` to those packages. Verified end-to-end: real `opa eval data.apt.break_glass` returns `{"allow_override": true, "deny": []}` (no `allow` key), and feeding that exact shape through `_eval_opa` returns `(False, 'OPA apt.break_glass deny: (no reason given)')` — i.e. a VALID override is DENIED. Same reproduced for kg_admission (clean mutation → deny) and taliban (unanimous approve → deny). sa_to_sp/sp_to_st/st_to_scw/fulfillment_gate/harness all define `allow` and work correctly.
fix: Make `_eval_opa` rule-name aware: try `allow`, then fall back to `allow_override`/`allow_mutation`/`approve` (or pass the expected decision key alongside each `_GATE_POLICY` entry, e.g. a tuple `(package, decision_rule)`). Alternatively query the specific rule path (`data.apt.break_glass.allow_override`) instead of the whole package. Then add real tests that eval each policy's actual decision key.
why: When OPA is enabled (APT_OPA_ENABLED=true), three of the most security-relevant gates are structurally broken: break-glass overrides can never be granted via /gate/check, every KG admission-control mutation is silently blocked regardless of legitimacy, and the constitutional-9 naesengmoon gate can never approve. The deny reason is the meaningless string '(no reason given)', so an operator gets a confusing block with no diagnostic. This is a correctness + enforcement failure in the commander essence (OPA/rego enforcement is supposed to be authoritative).

title: OPA enforcement test suite never exercises the 3 broken policies; _FakeOPA hardcodes the `allow` shape, hiding the key-name mismatch
evidence: engine/gate/tests/test_gate.py:145-164 `_FakeOPA.eval` always returns `{"result": {"allow": self._allow, "deny": [...]}}` — only the `allow` shape. Every OPA test (test_opa_allow_yields_pass:180, test_opa_deny_*:196, test_opa_unreachable_*:209, test_opa_enabled_unmapped_*:220) uses gate_name `sa_to_sp` or `G3.5`. grep over tests for `allow_override|allow_mutation|approve` and for any real OPA subprocess/Data-API integration returns nothing. test_opa_client.py also uses a MockTransport that returns `{"result": {"allow": ...}}`. 14/14 gate tests pass, giving false confidence.
fix: Add a real-OPA integration test (skip if `opa` binary absent) that runs `opa eval -d engine/gate/policies/` for each mapped gate and feeds the actual response through the endpoint, asserting break_glass/kg_admission/taliban can PASS on valid input. At minimum, parametrize _FakeOPA to emit the real per-policy decision key.
why: The hardcoded fake response shape makes the suite green while the real OPA contract is violated for 30% of mapped policies. A passing test suite that cannot detect a policy that always-denies is dishonest coverage — exactly the failure naesengmoon's oracle lens is supposed to catch.

title: Circuit breaker persists time.monotonic() to Redis but claims 'restart-survivable' / 'ISO timestamp' — breaks across host reboot
evidence: engine/gate/circuit_breaker.py:105 `self._r.set(self._key("opened_at"), str(time.monotonic()))` and reads it back at :79-80 `opened_at = float(_decode(opened_at_raw)); if time.monotonic() - opened_at >= OPEN_DURATION_S`. The docstring at :14 claims `opened_at → ISO timestamp`. README.md:16 and __init__.py:7 claim the FSM is 'restart-survivable'. `time.monotonic()` has an undefined reference point valid only within one boot session; after a machine reboot it resets toward 0, so a persisted (large) opened_at makes `now - opened_at` hugely negative → `>= 30s` is never true → the circuit is stuck OPEN forever for any gate that was OPEN at reboot.
fix: Use wall-clock `time.time()` for the persisted `opened_at` (and compute elapsed against `time.time()`), and update the docstring to match. Keep monotonic only for purely in-process timing. Consider Redis TTL (`ex=`) on the OPEN keys as a belt-and-suspenders auto-recovery.
why: The whole point of Redis-backed state is surviving restarts; the README sells this as the one fully-real layer. A gate stuck OPEN after a reboot fails-closed permanently (blocks all traffic in blocker mode, or floods WOULD_FAIL advisories), and the corrupt-OPEN reset (:75-78) only triggers when opened_at is missing, not when it's stale-monotonic.

title: Declared 500ms gate timeout (Layer 1) is never enforced; tenacity retry on _call_kg_with_retry is dead code
evidence: engine/gate/gate_endpoint.py:54 `GATE_TIMEOUT_S = 0.5  # Resilience4j-style 500ms` is defined but grep shows no `asyncio.wait_for`/timeout use anywhere in the endpoint. The module docstring (:1-9 in __init__.py) and README:48 advertise '[1] Resilience4j-style timeout (500ms)' as a real layer. `_call_kg_with_retry` (:223-238) is decorated `@retry(retry=retry_if_exception_type(TransientGateError))` but its body never raises TransientGateError (only returns (False, reason)), so the retry/backoff is unreachable. `_decide` (:280-285) awaits OPA / calls the sync stub with no timeout wrapper.
fix: Wrap `_decide` in `asyncio.wait_for(..., GATE_TIMEOUT_S)` and treat TimeoutError as a fail-closed backend error (record_failure). Either make the stub raise TransientGateError on transient conditions so the retry is live, or remove the dead retry decorator and TransientGateError to avoid a misleading claim.
why: A hanging OPA sidecar or slow backend has no endpoint-level deadline (only OPAClient's httpx 500ms, which does not cover the stub path or _decide orchestration), so a slow gate can hang the request beyond the advertised SLA and never trip the circuit via timeout. The advertised Polly/Resilience4j chain is partly fictional, which is a robustness + honesty gap.

title: /gate/break-glass route ignores the break_glass.rego policy: no actor/expiry/reason-length check, allowlists gate-names not actors
evidence: engine/gate/gate_endpoint.py:202-217 break_glass() only checks `set(payload.covers_gates) & req.app.state.allowlist` (in-process set `{"cluster-autoscaler", "essential-infra-pod"}` set at :100) and never validates `payload.actor`, `payload.expires_at`, or reason length. By contrast break_glass.rego:14-28 gates on `input.actor in allowed_emergency_overrides` (5 actors), `count(override_reason) >= 20`, and `time.now_ns() < override_expires_at`. The endpoint matches on gate-name where the policy matches on actor — divergent semantics, and the rego policy is never invoked by this route.
fix: Route break-glass through OPA `apt.break_glass` (fixing finding #1 first so allow_override is read), or replicate its checks inline: validate actor against the allowlist, enforce reason length >= 20, and reject if expires_at is in the past. Reconcile the gate-name vs actor allowlist semantics.
why: Any caller can mint a break-glass token for an allowlisted gate name with an arbitrary actor, empty-ish reason, and even an already-past expires_at (it is echoed back, not enforced). The richer, safer rego authz exists but is dead for this path, so the actual enforcement is far weaker than the policy implies — a real authz hole in an emergency-override endpoint.

title: Composition Root health/boot claims (Neo4j, structlog, KG allowlist) are stubbed but /gate/health reports success-shaped output
evidence: lifespan (gate_endpoint.py:98-100) leaves Neo4j connection as a comment ('실제 연결은 후속 sprint — 본 prototype은 stub') and hardcodes the allowlist set instead of loading KG `:BreakGlassAllowlist`. README.md:159-168 'Composition Root (eager validation)' lists Neo4j health check, KG node load, structlog setup as boot-time validations that fail startup if unmet ('위 5 중 하나라도 실패 → startup exception'). /gate/health (:132-139) returns redis/mode/allowlist_size with no Neo4j or structlog status. The endpoint docstring (:6-21) and README status table do disclose these as stubs, so this is a doc/claim-vs-reality drift, not a hidden bug.
fix: Trim the README 'Composition Root (eager validation)' section to match the honest status table (mark Neo4j/structlog/KG-allowlist load as Sprint-3 stubs), or implement the eager checks. Add a `neo4j`/`structlog` field to /gate/health reflecting actual (stub) status.
why: The README's eager-validation narrative overstates boot guarantees; an operator could assume Neo4j connectivity is verified at startup when it is not even attempted. The inline status table mitigates this, so severity is low, but the two docs sections contradict each other.

title: Resolver validate cannot flag single-digit bare magic numbers (9/7/8) — 3 of 5 core fields undetectable
evidence: engine/resolver/resolver.py:40 `INLINE_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![\w./])(\d{2,4})(?![\w./])")` requires 2-4 digits, but line 143 `if num in {"200", "500", "9", "7", "8"}:` includes single-digit 9/7/8. Verified: validate() on 'Taliban uses 9 lenses' / 'contract has 7 fields' / 'ST has 8 areas' → flagged=[] (regex never produces a 1-digit match), while 'sweet 200 lines' → ['200']. The CORE_MAGIC_FIELDS lens_count_constitutional=9, contract_default_fields=7, st_decision_areas=8 (cypher_kg_client.py:21-27) are exactly the single-digit values, so bare hardcoded drift for 3 of the 5 externalized magic fields can never be detected by the `validate` command that exists to catch it.
fix: Change the regex to `\d{1,4}` (and rely on the `{200,500,9,7,8}` allowlist to suppress noise), OR split into two checks: 2-4 digit regex for 200/500 plus a word-boundary single-digit check for 9/7/8. Add test cases for bare 9/7/8 to test_resolver.py (current tests only exercise 200/500).
why: The resolver's entire purpose (RFC A6.1) is to detect SKILL.md authors hardcoding magic numbers that should be `{{cfg.X}}` markers. For 60% of the core fields the bare-number check is a no-op, so a SKILL.md that drifts by writing a literal `9`/`7`/`8` instead of the marker passes validation cleanly — silent false-negative drift, the exact failure mode the gate is supposed to prevent.

title: Resolver and gate commands ignore MCP/--local KG backend that every other command honors
evidence: engine/resolver/cypher_kg_client.py:39-44 `KGConfig.from_env()` reads only `os.environ["NEO4J_URI"]` / `os.environ["NEO4J_PASSWORD"]`; resolver.py:74-81 boots only via this. grep shows zero `BHGMAN_KG_MCP_URL` / `local` handling in engine/resolver/*.py or engine/gate/*.py. Yet resolver.py:79 BOOT-FAIL message says '...or run via parent Claude MCP', and cmd_longinus (commands.py:441) plus make_kg_runners (runtime.py:189-191) both detect `BHGMAN_KG_MCP_URL`. So `bhgman-tool resolver/gate` cannot reach a bolt-firewalled KG via the MCP gateway nor use the bundled `--local` KG, unlike occam/hades/eureka/legion/jaebaeman/acquire/oracle.
fix: Either route resolver/gate KG access through `make_kg_runners()`/`_resolve_kg_runners()` like the rest of the CLI, or (cheaper) drop the misleading 'or run via parent Claude MCP' clause from the resolver BOOT-FAIL string so it stops promising a path that isn't wired.
why: Inconsistent backend support: in the documented airobotics-1 deployment (bolt closed, MCP open on :55013), the resolver/gate verbs are unusable while all KG-engine verbs work. The BOOT-FAIL message actively misleads the operator into thinking MCP is a supported fallback for the resolver when no such code path exists.

title: Dead usage-guard code in nargs="+" subcommand handlers (prom/tlb/longinus/jaebaeman/harness)
evidence: parser.py declares `topic`/`target`/`op`/`goal`/`action` with `nargs="+"` (e.g. line 91, 107, 129, 261, 140), so argparse raises SystemExit('the following arguments are required') before the handler runs. Verified: `parse_args(['prom'])` → SystemExit 2; `['tlb']`,`['longinus']`,`['jaebaeman']`,`['harness']` all SystemExit 2. Therefore the handler-internal guards — commands.py:362 `if not args.topic:`, :391 `if not args.target:`, :425 `if not args.op:`, :481 `if not args.action:`, :1264 `if not args.goal:` — are unreachable. (Only `apt` uses `nargs="*"`, so its commands.py:157 guard IS live and tested.)
fix: Either remove the dead `if not args.X` guards, or — if the richer usage strings are desired — switch those positionals to `nargs="*"` so the handler guard actually fires and prints the curated usage. Keep behavior consistent with `apt`.
why: Not a user-facing bug (the user still gets a usage error from argparse), but it is dead code that misleads readers into thinking the handlers are reachable empty, and the bespoke usage strings (which differ from argparse's) are never shown. Low maintenance hazard / coverage illusion.

title: cmd_status embeds KG password (incl. default) into argv passed to remote shell — process-list exposure
evidence: commands.py:719 `f"cypher-shell -u {shlex.quote(user)} -p {shlex.quote(password)} --format plain"` builds the ssh remote command with the literal password; password resolves (commands.py:659-664) to NEO4J_PASSWORD/SYMPOSIUM_KG_PASSWORD or the hardcoded default `"neo4jpassword"`. This string is the ssh argv, visible via `ps`/`/proc` on the local host and (after ssh) on the remote. The pre-change code (git HEAD commands.py:660) used remote-evaluated `${NEO4J_PASSWORD:-neo4j}`, which did NOT expose the local secret in argv.
fix: Pass the password to the remote cypher-shell via stdin or an env var injected over the ssh channel (`ssh host 'NEO4J_PASSWORD=... cypher-shell -u ... ...'` still exposes it; prefer `cypher-shell` reading NEO4J_PASSWORD from env, or feed `:param`/credentials via stdin). At minimum, drop the `"neo4jpassword"` hardcoded default in favor of a clear 'set NEO4J_PASSWORD' error.
why: Minor secret-in-argv exposure regression introduced by the in-flight change. Operationally low (operator-run CLI over Tailscale-internal hosts), but the hardcoded default `neo4jpassword` and the now-local-visible secret are a step down from the prior remote-only expansion.

title: Vestigial eureka/occam oracle_lens-collision regression test no longer exercises a real condition
evidence: test_main.py:312-327 test_eureka_runs_pipeline_even_after_occam_oracle_lens_cached deliberately `sys.path.insert(...engine/occam)` + `import oracle_lens` to reproduce a sys.modules bare-name collision, asserting eureka still runs. But runtime.py:234-244 `_load_engine_module` now uses absolute package import `importlib.import_module(f"engine.{subdir}.{module}")` and the docstring states `evict` is 'accepted for backward call-compat but no longer used'. So the collision the test simulates can no longer occur via bare-name sys.modules pollution; the test passes trivially and no longer guards the refactored code path. Callers commands.py:485 and :1356 still pass `evict=(...)` to a parameter that is a no-op.
fix: Either delete the now-moot test (the absolute-import design makes the collision impossible) or rewrite it to assert the absolute-import contract directly (e.g. that engine.occam.oracle_lens and engine.eureka.oracle_lens resolve to distinct modules). Drop the unused `evict=` arguments at commands.py:485/1356 and the parameter itself.
why: Gives false confidence: a green test implying the oracle_lens-collision is actively guarded when the underlying mechanism was removed. The dead `evict` argument at two call sites adds to the illusion.

title: kg_query write-keyword guard is an incomplete substring check — SET/DROP/CALL/LOAD CSV writes pass through with mutate=False
evidence: engine/mcp_server/tools/symposium.py:216-222 — has_write_keyword = any(kw in req.cypher.upper() for kw in ("CREATE", "MERGE", "DELETE", "REMOVE")). Verified live: _kg_query_impl(KGQueryRequest(cypher='MATCH (n) SET n.foo = 1', mutate=False)) is NOT blocked (blocked=False, passed straight to _ssh_cypher). Cypher's write surface also includes SET, DROP, FOREACH(...SET...), and write-capable CALL apoc.* procedures / LOAD CSV — none are in the keyword list. So a 'read-only' (mutate=False) call can mutate or destroy production KG data.
fix: Replace the substring check with a tokenized Cypher write-clause detector (word-boundary regex over the full write vocabulary: CREATE, MERGE, DELETE, REMOVE, SET, DROP, FOREACH, LOAD CSV, plus a CALL-procedure allowlist), or route reads through an EXPLAIN/access-mode='read' cypher-shell flag so the database itself enforces read-only. Add a parametrized test covering SET/DROP/CALL/LOAD CSV with mutate=False (currently absent).
why: kg_query is an MCP tool exposed to the agent/Claude-Code surface. Its sole safety mechanism for the read/write boundary is this keyword list. A SET (property overwrite) or DROP CONSTRAINT issued with mutate=False is silently executed against the live Neo4j as if read-only — exactly the destructive-op class the project gates behind explicit verdicts. This is a genuine write-safety hole, not a heuristic nicety.

title: kg_query write-guard false-positives: benign read queries containing a keyword as a substring are wrongly rejected
evidence: engine/mcp_server/tools/symposium.py:221-222 — `if not req.mutate and has_write_keyword: return {ok:False, reason:'write keyword detected...'}`. Verified live: read queries `MATCH (n) WHERE n.name="CREATEDBY" RETURN n`, `... n.status="DELETED" ...`, `... n.kind="MERGED_PR" ...`, `MATCH (n {label:"REMOVED"}) RETURN n` are ALL blocked (ok=False) because CREATE/DELETE/MERGE/REMOVE appear as substrings of literal/string values.
fix: Use word-boundary matching (re.search(r'\b(CREATE|MERGE|DELETE|REMOVE|SET|DROP|...)\b', cypher, re.I)) and ideally ignore string literals, so substrings inside identifiers/values do not trip the guard.
why: Legitimate KG reads whose data contains these common English-ish tokens (CREATEDBY, DELETED, MERGED, REMOVED — all plausible node labels/property values in this very codebase) are unusable through the tool, undermining the kg_query read path's correctness. The same root cause (substring vs token match) drives both this and the write-bypass finding.

title: git_oracle maps git copy ('C…') status to RENAME, mislabeling a copied file's truth-kind
evidence: git_oracle.py:109 `if (status.startswith("R") or status.startswith("C")) and len(parts) >= 3: return GitEvent(..., RENAME, path=parts[2], old_path=parts[1])`. A copy means the OLD path still exists on disk (unlike a rename/move), so feeding it as RENAME into `_git_true_kind` (git_oracle.py:139-140) would classify the source node as MOVE/MOVE_EDIT even though it was not moved — a wrong ground-truth label.

why: Copies are rare in this corpus so impact is small, but because this is a ground-truth oracle, any mislabel directly biases the longinus real-data classification-accuracy number. Conflating copy with rename is a semantic error in the very layer that is supposed to be the independent truth.

title: code_to_kg emits CodeExternal stub nodes for stdlib method calls (append/join), polluting the KG it claims to guard

title: kg_writer.to_cypher string escaping handles quote/backslash but not newlines/control chars
evidence: engine/code_to_kg/kg_writer.py:147-154 `_lit` only does `.replace('\\','\\\\').replace("'","\\'")`. A symbol name, qualname, or sourcePath containing a literal newline or other control character is interpolated raw into the generated Cypher string literal. Test test_to_cypher_is_escaped (test_kg_writer.py:51-55) only covers apostrophes. to_cypher builds raw Cypher strings (not parameterized) intended to be executed against the canonical Neo4j KG.
fix: Escape `\n`, `\r`, `\t` and other control chars in `_lit`, or (better) switch to_cypher to emit parameterized statements with a params dict rather than literal interpolation.
why: If an ingested file path or identifier contains a newline (possible via odd filenames or generated code), the emitted Cypher is malformed or could break out of the string literal. Low likelihood for normal Python identifiers, but the canonical-KG write path should not hand-roll string escaping.

title: LocalKgStore.add_edge resolves node index by value-equality, risking aliasing for empty/identical-content nodes
evidence: engine/kg_local/store.py:106-110 `add_edge` does `si, di = self.nodes.index(src), self.nodes.index(dst)`. list.index uses `==` (dict equality), not identity. Two distinct nodes with identical `{labels, props}` (e.g. two `{'labels':['Node'],'props':{}}` created by runner.py:113 `_hades_link_members` / runner.py:237 before a name is set) would resolve to the first match. merge_node keys protect most paths, but the store offers no identity guarantee and edges persist as integer indices that survive save/load.
fix: Use identity lookup (`next(i for i,n in enumerate(self.nodes) if n is src)`) in add_edge/out_edges, and add a regression test creating two empty-prop nodes before edging.
why: An edge intended for one node could attach to a value-equal duplicate, silently mis-wiring the local KG graph. Currently latent because all merge paths set a distinct key, but it is a fragile invariant with no test for the duplicate-empty-node case.
